pages.title: Muonic Catalyst
pages.text: A capsule of molecules in which electrons are replaced by muons, two hundred times heavier. The orbitals shrink accordingly, and two nuclei that would never fuse at room temperature are pulled close enough to tunnel into one. It feels oddly heavy for its size.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Muon-catalysed fusion was known in the 1950s; its problem is that muons are short-lived and get stuck. Using a noble gas clathrate to hold the fuel, quark-gluon plasma to make muons and a monopole to free them, I got the catalyst to work cycle after cycle.
